title: Genesis-aware restore record classification
description: Objective: keep disaster restore usable after a genesis authentication fence is installed. Deliverable: teach the production restore reader/controller to distinguish an exact canonical, anchored GENESIS binding from an InstalledRestoreRecord: a verified genesis row means no disaster restore is currently installed and may be replaced only by the existing verified atomic restore flow; any malformed, unknown, unanchored, or row/proof-mismatched ACTIVE payload remains fail-closed. Depends on task-2846816783104c52bfd4226782b10cc0's tagged canonical genesis proof and is a prerequisite for task-e19074f841f9450296799abfba9bfcaa. Current live proof: fresh createStoreDependencies followed by provider.restore().inspect() returns RESTORE_RECORD_UNREADABLE because readInstalledRestore assumes every ACTIVE payload is a restore record. NOT in scope: changing restore quiesce/reducer policy, two-slot anchor mechanics, minting genesis, session lifetime, or inventing decode-failure-as-absence. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run src/recovery/restore-controller.test.ts src/recovery/restore-controller-reachability.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: readInstalledRestore recognizes only a canonical genesis payload whose full public proof, row refs, binding digest, tagged project/store context, and durable genesis anchor all agree; it returns the exact non-installed/genesis state without claiming a disaster restore.

Malformed, truncated, alternate-version, unanchored, unknown, row-divergent, or hostile genesis-looking ACTIVE bytes still return RESTORE_RECORD_UNREADABLE at DAEMON_RESTORE_CONTROLLER (or the exact upstream store refusal), never ABSENT by decode failure.

A store with verified genesis can run the existing verified restore flow to QUIESCED/INSTALLED, atomically replacing genesis through the existing restore transaction; the old genesis refs no longer satisfy the authentication fence afterward.
An already restore-installed ACTIVE row retains byte-identical current behavior, replay/fence codes, and two-slot/anchor semantics; this task adds no second restore installer.

Generated strict-classification cases assert a nonzero exact count, and mutating the genesis discriminator/proof comparison or accepting generic decode failure reddens the production restore-boundary tests.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck and focused restore-controller tests exit 0.
taskRails: Never implement `decodeRestoreRecord(...) === null` as genesis/absence; genesis requires positive exact proof and anchor evidence.
Preserve restore-controller exact code/layer/component precedence and the existing atomic restore binding replacement.
Do not serialize or log raw nonce, private key, key handle, bearer, or proof-of-possession secret.
Keep new production logic in focused <=250-line modules; restore-controller.ts is already above target and must not grow toward 400.

implementationPlan.description: TDD. Make genesis PERSIST the full canonical binding instead of a bare digest. apps/daemon/src/identity/genesis-recovery-binding.ts:117 currently installs `payload: encoder.encode(binding.storeContextDigest)` - 64 hex chars, from which no reader can ever verify a signature. Replace it with `encodeBinding(binding)` from recovery-incarnation-binding-codec.js, which the dependency task landed precisely to carry this (the installer's own comment says so). The binding returned by mintGenesisIncarnation already carries publicKeySpkiHex, bindingDigest, proof, projectId and storeContextDigest, so nothing new is minted here - only what is written down changes. Do NOT touch mintGenesisIncarnation; minting genesis is out of scope. Keep every existing outcome (PRESENT / DEFERRED / INSTALLED), every GENESIS_RECOVERY_ERROR_CODE, and the read-back-judged install exactly as they are. Tests assert the installed payload round-trips through decodeBinding to a binding with origin 'GENESIS' and that no raw nonce, private key, PKCS8 or key handle appears in the persisted bytes.
implementationPlan.note:
Genesis now persists the full canonical binding. `payload: encoder.encode(binding.storeContextDigest)` (64 hex chars) replaced by `payload: encodeBinding(binding)` at genesis-recovery-binding.ts:118; the now-unused module `encoder` was dropped. mintGenesisIncarnation untouched. Every existing outcome (PRESENT/DEFERRED/INSTALLED), every GENESIS_RECOVERY_ERROR_CODE and the read-back-judged install are unchanged — all 8 pre-existing tests still pass.

TDD: 2 new tests written first and confirmed red for the right reason ("the persisted payload must decode canonically", and SyntaxError parsing 64 hex chars as JSON), then green. They assert the payload round-trips through decodeBinding to origin GENESIS carrying proof.verified/signatureHex/publicKeySpkiHex/bindingDigest, that storeContextDigest still equals the shared mint's, and that no privateKey/PKCS8/keyHandle/nonce substring appears — plus the EXACT 12-key set, so a future field cannot smuggle secret material past the substring list. New helper capturedGenesisPayload() refuses the install on purpose so it stays on the pre-install path regardless of what the installer does after a successful write.

MEASUREMENT that changes step 3 — the architect flagged this as unresolved and it resolves AGAINST asserting equality. `read.bindingDigest` is NOT `binding.bindingDigest`. The store computes it as sha256 over frame([slot, incarnationRef, keyEpochRef, installedAt, payload]) (recovery-install-codec.ts:109-115, surfaced via recovery-install.ts:132 `bindingDigest: encoded.digest`). The mint's is digestOf("binding", schemaVersion, ...contextParts, incarnationDigest, incarnationRef, keyEpochRef, verificationKeyFingerprint, publicKeySpkiHex) (recovery-incarnation-context.ts:158). Different domains, different inputs — requiring equality would refuse every valid genesis. Step 3 conjunct (3) will instead RECOMPUTE the derivation through deriveIncarnation + snapshotGenesisContext and require the binding's own bindingDigest/incarnationRef/keyEpochRef/challengeDigest match, which is what "recomputes from its contents" has to mean and which folds in conjunct (4) since contextParts covers projectId and storeContextDigest.

BLOCKER FOUND for step 3 conjunct (5), reported now rather than at step 3: readAnchoredIncarnation CANNOT be used to verify a genesis anchor. It hard-filters `binding.origin !== "RESTORE"` (recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts:81) and its own doc comment says "A future genesis anchor needs its own reader." Step 2 will therefore also generalize that module and export a genesis reader; anchorIncarnation's own idempotence lookup (:115) has the same RESTORE-only blindness, which would make a second genesis anchor hit the expectedVersion-0 conflict and return false.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/identity/genesis-recovery-binding.test.ts -> 10 passed (10), exit 0.

NOTE ON THE TASK'S NAMED COMMAND: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run <path>` exits 1 with "No test files found" — it resolves the ROOT vitest config, whose include is adapters/**,packages/**,tests/** and excludes apps/**. The daemon's own test script is `vitest run --root . --config package.json src`; the `--config package.json` is what drops the root include. I will run the named command in that working form at step 10 and disclose the substitution rather than paper over an exit 1.

implementationPlan.description: TDD. Give genesis the DURABLE ANCHOR that DoD-1 requires it to agree with. I measured that no production site anchors a genesis incarnation: anchorIncarnation has production callers only on the restore/succession paths (recovery-key-provider.ts:120 and :149, recovery-succession.ts:351), and genesis only READS anchors via hasAnchoredIncarnation to defer to a pending restore. Call anchorIncarnation(store, request, binding) from the genesis installer AFTER a successful install and read-back. DERIVE the RecoveryDurableWriteRequest {correlationId, decidedAt, principalId, projectId} INSIDE the installer - decidedAt from the existing config.clock(), projectId from config, and correlationId/principalId as fixed deterministic genesis values (e.g. derived from binding.incarnationRef). Do NOT add them to GenesisRecoveryConfig: that would force a change in daemon-store-dependencies.ts:98, and caller-selected identity is exactly what the genesis context discipline forbids. Widen the GenesisBindingStore interface by the one store capability anchorIncarnation needs. NOTE the existing invariant you are changing: after this, hasAnchoredIncarnation becomes true for a genesis store, so a later call with a CLEARED binding slot will DEFER rather than re-mint. Assert that deliberately in a test - it is the correct behavior (a store with recovery history must not be re-fenced) but it must be a recorded decision, not an accident.
implementationPlan.note:
Genesis now writes a durable anchor. Four new tests, all confirmed RED by drill before being accepted (see drill below).

PLAN DEVIATION, forced, and it is the blocker I flagged in step 1. The plan said "call anchorIncarnation" as if the existing reader would then see the row. It would not: readAnchoredIncarnation hard-filtered `binding.origin !== "RESTORE"` and its own doc comment said "A future genesis anchor needs its own reader." Worse, anchorIncarnation's OWN idempotence lookup (:115) used that same restore-only reader, so a genesis re-anchor would have found nothing, fallen through to a second write, and been refused by the expectedVersion-0 conflict — an idempotent retry reported as a failure. So recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts was generalized:
- new private readAnchoredBindingOfOrigin(store, projectId, ref, origin) — the one scan, origin as a FILTER;
- readAnchoredIncarnation keeps its exact RESTORE-only signature and behavior, now a thin wrapper;
- new readAnchoredGenesisIncarnation returning GenesisIncarnationBinding | null — a separate export on purpose, since a restore caller receiving genesis rows would read restoreCommandId off a store that never restored;
- anchorIncarnation looks up under binding.origin;
- store params narrowed to new AnchorDecisionReader / AnchorDecisionWriter (Pick<SqliteEventStore,...>) so GenesisBindingStore can satisfy them without the whole event store. Narrowing a param accepts strictly more, so existing callers are unaffected.

Installer: GenesisBindingStore extends AnchorDecisionWriter (the one added capability is commitExpectedVersionDecision); GenesisRecoveryConfig deliberately NOT widened, so daemon-store-dependencies.ts:98 is untouched and stays with its owner task-e19074f8. anchorRequestFor derives {correlationId: `genesis-recovery:${incarnationRef}`, decidedAt: config.clock(), principalId: "daemon-genesis", projectId} — both new fields are functions of the incarnation, so a retry after a crash reproduces the same command key.

SECOND DEVIATION, deliberate: the anchor is driven from the read-back SLOT BYTES in a shared settle() covering both the INSTALLED and PRESENT paths, not only after a fresh install as the plan worded it. Reason: if the install lands and the anchor does not, the next boot sees a PRESENT slot, never mints again, and the fence is stranded unanchored FOREVER — permanently unclassifiable. settle() heals that. It is not a second installer: it writes no binding, and anchorIncarnation recognises the repeat by byte equality and commits nothing (asserted: anchorRowCount stays 1 across two boots). A slot this module did not write — a restore record, or a genesis payload whose refs disagree with its row — is returned exactly as before and never anchored.

New stable code GENESIS_ANCHOR_REFUSED (storeCode ANCHOR_NOT_COMMITTED) rather than reporting INSTALLED on an uncommitted anchor; no try/catch was added, so a genuine store fault still throws, matching anchorIncarnation's documented contract.

THE INVARIANT CHANGE IS ASSERTED, not discovered: test "DEFERS rather than re-minting once its own anchor exists and the slot is cleared" drives the REAL anchor rows through the real reader with only the slot cleared, and asserts installs === 0 and outcome DEFERRED. Correct — a store fenced once must not be silently re-fenced — and now recorded.

MUTATION DRILL (proves the tests are not vacuous): inserted `if (decoded !== null) return present(outcome, current);` immediately before the anchorIncarnation call, printed the applied line (137), chained with &&. Exactly the 4 new tests went red, each on its own assertion: "expected null not to be null", "expected +0 to be 1", "must not re-mint over recovery history", "expected true to be false". Restored with Edit, not git checkout, and sha256sum -c verified the file back to pre-drill bytes: OK.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec tsc --project tsconfig.json -> exit 0. pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/identity/ src/recovery/ -> 23 files, 435 passed (435), exit 0. Restore/succession/inventory callers of the generalized anchor are all in that run and unchanged.

Sizes: genesis-recovery-binding.ts 189, recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts 193 — both under the 250 target (grep -c '').

implementationPlan.description: TDD. Create the classification module - a NEW focused file, because task rail 4 forbids growing restore-controller.ts (284 lines, already above the 250 target). Export a classifier that takes the store, the projectId and the ACTIVE row read, and returns an exact discriminated result. The GENESIS arm requires POSITIVE EXACT PROOF of ALL FIVE conjuncts, every one of which must be checked: (1) decodeBinding(payload) returns non-null AND binding.origin === 'GENESIS'; (2) binding.incarnationRef === row.incarnationRef AND binding.keyEpochRef === row.keyEpochRef; (3) the binding's own bindingDigest recomputes from its contents - FIRST VERIFY what the store computes read.bindingDigest over, because it may be a digest of the payload BYTES rather than the binding's internal bindingDigest, in which case requiring equality between the two would be simply wrong; (4) binding.projectId and binding.storeContextDigest agree with the daemon's asserted project identity, recomputed through the landed context helper rather than trusted from the payload; (5) readAnchoredIncarnation(store, projectId, binding.incarnationRef) returns a binding whose encodeBinding bytes are byte-equal to the row payload, mirroring anchorIncarnation's own sameBytes idempotence check. ANY conjunct failing is a refusal, never a genesis and never an absence. Per task rail 1, `decodeBinding(...) === null` is NEVER genesis and NEVER absence - it is unreadable.
implementationPlan.note:
New module apps/daemon/src/recovery/restore-genesis-classifier.ts — 145 lines, well under the 250 target — plus its .js bridge (recovery/ carries a bridge for every one of its 31 production .ts files; vitest and tsc are both blind to a missing one).

classifyGenesisFence(store: AnchorDecisionReader, projectId, row) returns a discriminated GenesisFenceVerdict: {verified: true, binding} or {verified: false, reason} over 8 stable GENESIS_FENCE_REJECTIONS. A reason rather than a bare boolean so the sweep in step 8 and the refusal tests in step 6 can pin WHICH conjunct refused instead of merely that something did.

CONJUNCT (3) RESOLVED AS MEASURED, NOT AS WORDED. The plan told me to verify what the store computes read.bindingDigest over before asserting equality; it is sha256 over frame([slot, incarnationRef, keyEpochRef, installedAt, payload]) — the ROW — while binding.bindingDigest covers the derivation inputs. Equality between them would refuse every valid genesis, so it is NOT asserted. Instead the derivation is RECOMPUTED through the landed helpers: snapshotGenesisContext({projectId}) rebuilds the context from the daemon's asserted identity, then deriveIncarnation must reproduce incarnationRef, keyEpochRef, bindingDigest AND proof.challengeDigest. That subsumes conjunct (4) since contextParts covers projectId and storeContextDigest. The row digest is not skipped, it is enforced upstream — the store refuses the read with RECOVERY_BINDING_DIGEST_MISMATCH before these bytes reach the classifier — and the module comment records that.

CONJUNCT (5) uses readAnchoredGenesisIncarnation, the reader step 2 had to add; readAnchoredIncarnation is RESTORE-only and would have answered null for every genesis. Byte-equality mirrors anchorIncarnation's own sameBytes check.

TWO CONJUNCTS BEYOND THE PLAN'S FIVE, both inside DoD-1's "full public proof", both cheap:
- PROOF_UNVERIFIED — the Ed25519 signature is actually VERIFIED through the published SPKI, not merely read as a structural `verified: true` flag. decodeBinding checks the flag's shape; a flag is a claim, the signature is the proof. Verification runs through nodeGenesisCryptoShell, the same shell the mint verified with, and a throw on a malformed key is caught as a failed proof rather than escaping a read path that must fail closed.
- The verificationKeyFingerprint is re-derived as digestOf("key", spki). It is the one derivation input nothing else pins, so without this a binding could carry a fingerprint unrelated to the key that signs it.

Recorded in the module comment, because it matters for how QA reads this: every conjunct except the anchor is computable by anyone holding the project id — a genesis binding proves itself with a key it minted for itself, so a forger can build a self-consistent one at will. The ANCHOR is the only conjunct a forger cannot satisfy, because it requires a durable command-decision row this daemon committed. That is why ANCHOR_ABSENT is a hard refusal and not a soft one.

Rail 1 is honoured at the first line of the function: decodeBinding(...) === null returns PAYLOAD_UNDECODABLE. Never genesis, never absence. Step 9's third drill will prove that guard is live.

TDD: 4 tests appended to restore-controller.test.ts (the production restore-boundary suite the DoD names, and the file the task's own verification command runs — a separate file would have sat outside it). New harness helper genesisFixture(label) drives the PRODUCTION installer and reads back the row it actually wrote; nothing hand-installs a payload, since such a fixture proves the decoder while leaving the installer — the half that produced the original live symptom — untested. Cases: the real production fence verifies; three undecodable payloads (bad JSON, truncated, binary) all return PAYLOAD_UNDECODABLE; a freshly minted but never-anchored binding returns ANCHOR_ABSENT even though it proves itself perfectly; the same row classified against "project-elsewhere" returns PROJECT_CONTEXT_MISMATCH.

The passing case is itself evidence step 2 works end to end: it can only reach verified:true because the production installer anchored the fence.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec tsc --project tsconfig.json -> exit 0; vitest run --root . --config package.json src/recovery/restore-controller.test.ts -> 33 passed (33), exit 0. restore-controller.ts itself is untouched so far — wiring is step 5.

implementationPlan.note:
One arm added to RestoreInspection and nothing else:

  | { readonly incarnationRef: string; readonly keyEpochRef: string;

implementationPlan.description: Wire readInstalledRestore to the classifier while keeping the restore path BYTE-IDENTICAL, which DoD-4 requires. Preserve the existing order of operations exactly: the store read and its two catch arms, the !read.ok refusal, and the ABSENT arm all stay as they are. Then attempt decodeRestoreRecord FIRST and, when it yields a record whose incarnationRef and keyEpochRef match the row, return the INSTALLED result unchanged - that ordering guarantees an already-restore-installed row takes a path this task did not modify, rather than relying on a reviewer to compare two branches. ONLY when the restore decode fails does the genesis classifier run. If the classifier verifies genesis, return the new arm; otherwise return controllerRefusal('RESTORE_RECORD_UNREADABLE') exactly as today. Preserve the existing exact code/layer/component precedence: an upstream store refusal still surfaces verbatim via restoreRefusal(read.layer, read.code) and is never flattened into the controller's own code. restore-controller.ts must NOT grow toward 400 - delegate, do not inline; net line change should be near zero.
implementationPlan.note:
Wired, with the restore path changed by exactly ONE line. The full diff of readInstalledRestore's body is:

-  if (record === null) return controllerRefusal("RESTORE_RECORD_UNREADABLE");
+  if (record === null) return inspectGenesisFence(store, projectId, read.binding);

Everything a restore-installed row touches is byte-identical and I diffed it to confirm: the store read, both catch arms (DurableStoreError -> restoreRefusal("DURABLE_STORE", ...), otherwise controllerRefusal), the !read.ok verbatim restoreRefusal(read.layer, read.code), the ABSENT arm, decodeRestoreRecord running FIRST, the ref-divergence refusal, and the INSTALLED return. DoD-4 holds by construction, not by a reviewer comparing branches — an already-restore-installed row never enters code this task wrote.

RAIL 1: this is NOT "null means genesis". inspectGenesisFence returns controllerRefusal("RESTORE_RECORD_UNREADABLE") — the same code at the same DAEMON_RESTORE_CONTROLLER layer as before — unless all conjuncts prove out. A comment says so at the call site, because that line is otherwise exactly the shape rail 1 forbids and a reviewer should not have to open another file to tell them apart. Step 9's drill 3 proves the guard is live.

The classifier needs the asserted projectId and readInstalledRestore only took the store; SqliteEventStore exposes no projectId getter (grepped: openForProject consumes it, nothing publishes it). That pulls restore-controller-commands.ts into the task's files — beyond the plan's list, forced by the missing parameter, and it is a 3-line change.

No second installer was added. discardSnapshottedRestore deliberately lets GENESIS_FENCED fall through with ABSENT — a fence is not a settled restore, so RESTORE_ALREADY_SETTLED still fires only for a real INSTALLED row. Both are commented.

inspectGenesisFence (the RestoreInspection adapter) lives in the classifier module, not inlined, so restore-controller.ts stayed thin: 284 -> 294 lines, of which 7 are the two review comments and 3 are the widened signature. implementationPlan.description: TDD. Cover the hostile and near-miss refusal cases DoD-2 names, each asserting the EXACT code AND the layer/component, never merely that the call refused. Cases: malformed bytes; truncated bytes; a valid binding with origin 'RESTORE' in the ACTIVE slot where a genesis is expected; an alternate/unknown schemaVersion; a genesis binding whose incarnationRef or keyEpochRef diverges from the row; a genesis binding whose projectId or storeContextDigest does not recompute; a genesis binding with NO anchor row; a genesis binding whose anchor row carries different bytes; and a hostile genesis-LOOKING payload that is shaped correctly but fails exactly one conjunct. Every one must return RESTORE_RECORD_UNREADABLE at DAEMON_RESTORE_CONTROLLER (or the exact upstream store refusal where the store answers first) and NEVER ABSENT. Because two layers can refuse here, assert WHICH layer answered - a test that only asserts 'refused' passes even after a second guard starts answering first, and this task adds exactly such a second guard.
implementationPlan.note:
12 hostile/near-miss cases as a table (FENCE_CASES), each driven through the OPERATOR PORT — createRestorePort(store, PROJECT_ID).inspect() — after a real installRecoveryBinding into the ACTIVE slot, plus 2 layer-discrimination tests. Every case in the DoD-2 list is present:

DECODES  -> malformed bytes; truncated bytes; alternate schemaVersion  => PAYLOAD_UNDECODABLE
ORIGIN   -> a REAL RESTORE binding (minted through the production incarnation service, not hand-shaped) in the ACTIVE slot => ORIGIN_NOT_GENESIS
ROW_REFS -> incarnationRef diverges from its row; keyEpochRef diverges => ROW_REFS_DIVERGE
PROJECT_CONTEXT -> storeContextDigest that does not recompute; a projectId the daemon did not assert => PROJECT_CONTEXT_MISMATCH
DERIVATION -> verificationKeyFingerprint unrelated to its own public key => DERIVATION_MISMATCH
PROOF    -> a forged signature over a genuine challenge, same length and still hex so the codec admits it => PROOF_UNVERIFIED
ANCHOR   -> a perfectly self-proving binding the daemon never anchored => ANCHOR_ABSENT; non-canonical bytes that decode to the anchored binding => ANCHOR_BYTES_DIVERGE

Each case asserts THREE things, not one: the exact controller code AND layer via expectRefusal(inspection, RESTORE_CONTROLLER_LAYER, "RESTORE_RECORD_UNREADABLE"); that it is not ok and NOT outcome ABSENT; and the exact classifier conjunct via classifyGenesisFence, so a case cannot silently drift onto a different guard than the one it was written for.

EVERY CASE IS VALID AT ITS EARLIER LAYERS, which is what makes it reach the guard it names. The tampered digests are all still 64-hex so decodeBinding admits them; the forged signature keeps its length and hex alphabet; the non-canonical case is the SAME fields with reversed key order, so it decodes to a byte-identical binding and passes conjuncts 1-5, leaving only the byte comparison to refuse. That last case is the one that proves the anchor comparison is a real byte check rather than a decode-and-compare.

TWO LAYERS CAN REFUSE HERE, so the discrimination is asserted directly: closing the store makes the read throw DurableStoreError and the inspection comes back at layer DURABLE_STORE with code STORE_CLOSED — and the test explicitly asserts it is NOT at DAEMON_RESTORE_CONTROLLER and NOT RESTORE_RECORD_UNREADABLE. Without that, the controller could start swallowing store faults into its own code and every refusal test would stay green.

Also added the positive port test: a fenced store inspects to exactly {incarnationRef, keyEpochRef, ok: true, outcome: "GENESIS_FENCED"}, frozen — asserted with toEqual, so an extra field would fail.

FIXTURE BUG I HIT AND FIXED, worth recording: the first run had all 12 cases fail with RECOVERY_INCARNATION_INPUT_INVALID, not from the code under test but because I built the restore command id from the human-readable case NAME, and isCommandId refuses whitespace. Switched to an index, and added expect(index).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0) so a lookup that stopped resolving cannot silently produce "restore-cmd--1".

New harness helper mintRestoreIncarnation() mints through the production service. genesisFixture is reused per case, so each case runs against a store whose REAL genesis anchor exists — which is exactly what lets ANCHOR_BYTES_DIVERGE be distinguishable from ANCHOR_ABSENT.

implementationPlan.description: TDD. Prove the two behaviors that only show up end to end. (a) DoD-3: a store with a verified genesis binding can run the EXISTING verified restore flow through to QUIESCED/INSTALLED, atomically replacing genesis through the existing restore transaction, and the old genesis refs no longer satisfy the authentication fence afterwards - assert the post-restore refusal for an old-genesis credential by its exact code and layer. Use the existing restore flow; this task adds NO second restore installer. (b) DoD-1's reachability: extend restore-controller-reachability.test.ts so a FRESH store built the way production builds one reaches the genesis arm rather than RESTORE_RECORD_UNREADABLE - that failure was the task's original live symptom and this test is what proves it is gone. planningNotes.risks:
READ.BINDINGDIGEST MAY NOT BE THE BINDING'S BINDINGDIGEST. Step 3 conjunct (3) says to verify this FIRST. The store computes read.bindingDigest itself, plausibly over the payload BYTES, while binding.bindingDigest is the mint's digest over the binding's contents. If they are different digests, asserting equality is simply wrong and would refuse every valid genesis. Measure before asserting; I did not resolve this and am not guessing.

THE ANCHOR WRITE CHANGES AN EXISTING INVARIANT. Genesis currently installs only when hasAnchoredIncarnation is false. After step 2, a genesis store HAS an anchor, so a later call with a cleared binding slot DEFERS instead of re-minting. I believe that is correct - a store with recovery history must not be silently re-fenced - but it must be asserted as a deliberate test, not discovered later. Also confirm the second-boot path is idempotent: anchorIncarnation is single-shot on expectedVersion 0 and returns false on the version conflict, so a re-anchor of identical bytes must not be treated as a failure.

RAIL 1 IS THE EASIEST THING TO GET WRONG HERE. `decodeRestoreRecord(...) === null` already means 'unreadable' in the current code. It is one small step from there to writing `if (record === null) return genesis` - which is exactly the forbidden decode-failure-as-absence. Genesis requires POSITIVE exact proof of all five conjuncts. The step-9 drill exists specifically to prove this guard is real.

A REFUSAL TEST CAN BE ANSWERED BY THE WRONG LAYER. This task adds a SECOND guard behind the existing one. A test asserting only 'refused' stays green while the new guard silently starts answering first and the original is never exercised. Assert WHICH layer answered, on every refusal case.

A DEVIATION FIXTURE MUST BE VALID AT EARLIER LAYERS. A near-miss genesis payload that is malformed JSON never reaches the conjunct it was written to test - the decode refuses first. Each single-conjunct-failure case must be well formed everywhere else.

HAND-INSTALLED FIXTURES PROVE THE DECODER, NOT THE INSTALLER. The reachability test must build the store the way production does, or it certifies a path production never takes - which is how the original live symptom survived a green suite.
